Running the app

Nothing needs installing beyond Node. The API starts its own database, its own job queue, and seeds a demo team, so the first run works with no configuration.

npm install
npm run dev     # app on :3000, API on :4000

The first start downloads a database binary and a small embedding model, then caches both. Later starts take a few seconds.

Demo data is not persistent by default

Without a database URL the app runs an in-memory database, so restarting clears everything and reseeds. That is deliberate for a trial. See Configuration to point it at a real database.

Accounts and joining

There is no public sign-up. People join by invitation only, which is the right default for a private sales tool.

The very first account

An instance with no accounts shows a one-time setup screen. Whoever completes it becomes the administrator and can then invite everyone else. It is refused the moment any account exists, so the screen cannot be replayed.

You will not normally see this

The demo seed fills an empty database with three accounts, so the setup screen is skipped. Set SEED_ON_START=false for a real deployment and you will get it instead.

Inviting a colleague

An administrator invites from Admin → Team. Enter an address, optionally a name, and choose whether they join as a member or an administrator.

It works without an email server

With SMTP_URL configured the link is emailed. Without it the app says so plainly and shows you the link to pass on yourself, so invitations are never blocked on mail setup.

Joining

The invitee opens the link, which works while signed out, and chooses their own password. Nobody else ever knows it.

The link then stops working. It is single-use, expires after seven days, and is cancelled if a newer invitation is issued for the same address.

Roles and removal

Administrators can change anyone's role and remove accounts from the Team screen. Three rails stop an instance being broken by accident: the last administrator cannot be demoted or removed, you cannot demote or remove yourself, and nobody who still owns records can be removed until their work is reassigned.

ControlWhereWhat it does
EmailInvite formWho to invite. Refused if they already have an account.
NameInvite formOptional. Pre-fills their name so the invitation reads personally.

Copy linkAfter invitingCopies the invitation link to the clipboard.
ResendPending invitationsIssues a fresh link and cancels the previous one.
Bin iconPending invitationsRevokes the invitation. Their link stops working immediately.
Role dropdownPeoplePromotes or demotes. Refused for the last administrator.
Bin iconPeopleRemoves the account. Refused while they still own records.

Sessions

The session is a signed token in a cookie JavaScript cannot read, valid for seven days. Visiting any page while signed out sends you here and returns you afterwards.

The interface

Three fixed areas, so nothing moves under you as you scroll.

The left rail

Always visible and never scrolls away. A sparkle marks the screens where the AI does the work. The Admin group only appears for administrators.

The status pill

The single source of truth for whether AI is live. Amber with AI offline means the app is running on its built-in fallbacks; green with a model name means Claude is answering. Hover it for the embedding model, vector store and queue in use.

Your account

The button at the top right shows your initials, name and role. It opens a menu with your email address and Sign out.

Light and dark

The app follows your system setting. There is no theme switch to find.

Inside a deal

The header

Title, score ring and risk badge, then the contact, company and time since last activity. Four actions sit on the right: Draft follow-up, Summarize meeting, Edit, and the delete icon.

Timeline and notes

The record of everything that happened, on both deals and contacts.

Logging an entry

Type in the composer, choose the kind, and add it. Ctrl+Enter saves without reaching for the mouse.

Three things then happen in the background, and none of them make you wait: the note is classified for sentiment, embedded for semantic search, and the deal is re-scored and re-checked for risk.

Entry kinds

KindUse it forCounts as engagement
NoteAnything written downYes
CallA phone conversationYes
EmailCorrespondence, added automatically when you send from the appYes
MeetingA meeting, added automatically by the summarizerYes
SystemStage changes and merges, written by the appNo
The flagged marker

A note containing instruction-like text is marked flagged. The content is kept and shown in full. The marker only tells you the text looked like an attempt to steer the AI, which the app treats strictly as data.

ControlWhereWhat it does

TimestampEach entryHover for the exact date and time.
Sentiment labelEach entryHover for the reasoning and whether it came from Claude or the keyword fallback.

Tasks

Follow-ups, either typed by you or extracted from a meeting transcript.

Adding one

Type a title, optionally pick a due date, and press the + button or Enter.

Completing one

Tick the checkbox. The title strikes through immediately, and on the dashboard the row collapses out of the list.

Overdue dates turn red, and anything due within two days turns amber. The Tasks screen collects everything across your records.

ControlWhereWhat it does

Lead scoring

Every deal carries a score from 0 to 100 estimating how likely it is to close, drawn as a ring so you can read the pipeline without reading numbers.

BandRing colourMeans
70 to 100GreenStrong. Push to close.
40 to 69AmberLive, needs work.
Below 40GreyCold or stalling.

Hover any ring for the breakdown. Six components add up, each shown with the input that produced it.

ComponentRangeWhat moves it
Stage prior0 to 60How far along the pipeline the deal is
Recency0 to 12Days since anyone touched it
Deal value0 to 6Size, on a log scale, so big deals do not dominate
Stage velocity−15 to 6Time in the current stage against that stage's threshold
Note sentiment−12 to 12Recent note sentiment, weighted toward the newest, plus a trend adjustment
Engagement0 to 5Human touches in the last 30 days

Won is always 100 and Lost always 0. The score recalculates whenever the deal or its notes change, and a nightly pass refreshes recency so untouched deals cool off on their own.

Why the model is arithmetic, not a prediction

The formula is deterministic so it can be tested, costs nothing to re-run, and can always be explained to whoever disagrees with it. The AI's contribution is the sentiment of each note, which feeds one component.

Draft follow-up

On any deal or contact, Draft follow-up writes the next email for you.

  1. Optionally say what the email should do, for example "nudge on the revised pricing".
  2. Pick a tone: professional, friendly or concise.
  3. Generate. The model reads the contact, the deal and its stage, the last eight timeline entries, open tasks and the most recent meeting summary.
  4. Edit the subject and body freely. They are ordinary text boxes.
  5. Send & log to timeline, or copy it, or open it in your mail client.
Nothing is ever sent automatically

The AI only ever fills the box. Sending is always a click you make, and the sent email is written to the timeline so the history stays complete.

ControlWhereWhat it does
Purpose fieldTop of the dialogOptional steer for what the email should achieve.
Tone dropdownTop of the dialogProfessional, friendly or concise.
Generate / RegenerateTop of the dialogWrites a draft. Becomes Regenerate once one exists.

To / Subject / BodyThe draftAll editable before sending.

Ask your CRM

Type a question about your pipeline and get a filtered table back, not a paragraph.

Every answer shows the query that actually ran as a row of chips, so you can always check the machine understood you.

Questions it answers well

  • Show me deals over $10k closing this month
  • Which contacts have not been touched in 30 days?
  • My at-risk deals, biggest first
  • Open deals in negotiation with a score above 70
  • Contacts at Northwind tagged enterprise

What it refuses

Anything that writes, deletes or sends. Anything needing analysis it cannot express as a filter. Anything unrelated to the CRM. It says so plainly rather than guessing.

The model never touches the database

It proposes a small typed filter. The server checks every field and operator against a fixed allowlist, resolves the dates, rejects anything shaped like an injection, then runs a read-only query with your own access scope applied. A member cannot widen their view by asking nicely.

ControlWhereWhat it does
Question boxTopYour question. Enter or Ask submits.
AskTopSubmits. Disabled while empty.
Example chipsUnder the boxFill and run that question immediately.
Filter chipsEach answerThe validated query that actually ran.
Result rowsEach answerClick through to the deal or contact.

Semantic search

Search notes by meaning rather than keyword. Describe the situation you are trying to find.

Searching pricing pushback surfaces "budget has been cut for this quarter" and "the quote is about 30% above their budget line", neither of which contains a word from the query.

BadgeMeans
Semantic matchReal meaning-based search over embeddings
Keyword fallbackThe embedding model or vector store was unavailable, so plain text search ran instead. The reason is shown next to the badge.
ControlWhereWhat it does
Search boxTopSearches as you type, after a short pause.
Example chipsUnder the boxFill the box with that phrase.
Match percentageEach resultHow close the note is to your query.
Deal / contact linkEach resultOpens the record the note belongs to.

Duplicate detection

Admin only. New and edited contacts are checked automatically, and a full sweep runs nightly. Likely duplicates land in a review queue rather than being merged.

The matcher is built for the ways duplicates actually happen: a typo in an email, a mistyped domain, a nickname, a swapped name order, a reformatted phone, a company written two ways. Two different people at the same company are not duplicates and are not flagged.

Reviewing a pair

  • Keep this one on the record you want to survive. Deals, notes, tasks and meetings move across, empty fields are filled from the other record, tags are combined, and the merge is logged on the timeline.
  • Not a duplicate dismisses the pair so it stops coming back.
Merging never happens on its own

The queue is a suggestion. A person always picks the survivor, and the app asks for confirmation first. The retired record is hidden rather than deleted, so older links still resolve.

ControlWhereWhat it does
Scan all contactsTop rightQueues a full sweep instead of waiting for the nightly one.
Match percentageEach pairHow confident the matcher is.
ReasonsEach pairThe specific signals that matched, such as a mistyped domain.
Keep this oneEach recordMerges the other record into this one, after confirming.
Not a duplicateEach pairDismisses the pair permanently.
Contact nameEach recordOpens that contact in full.

Risk flagging

Open deals are checked on every change and again by a daily scan. Four signals can fire.

SignalFires when
StalledThe deal has sat in its stage past that stage's threshold, 14 days early on and 21 later
InactiveNobody has touched it for longer than the inactivity window, 14 days by default
Sentiment negativeRecent notes are negative, or sentiment has dropped sharply against older notes
Closing soon, unreadyThe close date is within a week but the deal is still early stage

Flagged deals collect at the top of the dashboard, each with a plain-English reason and a suggested next step. When AI is on, Claude writes that explanation from the actual notes. When it is off, you get the rule-based version, which is shorter but just as specific.

A deal drops off the list as soon as the underlying signals clear. Won and Lost deals are never flagged.

AI usage and cost

Admin only. Every AI call is logged: tokens in and out, cache reads, latency, status and an estimated cost.

Statuses

StatusMeans
okA real model call, billed
cachedServed from the response cache. No tokens, no cost
fallbackNo provider configured, so the built-in path ran
error / timeoutThe call failed and the feature degraded

The provider card shows the circuit breaker. After repeated failures it opens and calls fail fast instead of hanging, then recovers on its own. Reset clears it immediately.

ControlWhereWhat it does
Window dropdownTop right1, 7, 30 or 90 days.
ResetProvider cardCloses an open circuit breaker immediately. Only shown when it is not closed.
risk-scanBackground jobsRe-checks every open deal for risk.
rescoreBackground jobsRefreshes every score.
dedupe-scanBackground jobsFull duplicate sweep.

Background jobs

Work that would make you wait happens off the request. Scoring, sentiment, embedding, summarizing, duplicate checks and risk assessment all run as jobs, and rapid edits to one record collapse into a single job.

Scheduled jobRunsDoes
Risk scanDaily, 6amRe-checks every open deal for risk signals
RescoreDaily, 5amRefreshes scores so untouched deals cool off
Duplicate sweepDaily, 5.30amFull pass over contacts

Configuration

Copy .env.example to .env. Every setting has a working default; the ones below are worth changing.

Turning on Claude

ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...
ANTHROPIC_MODEL=claude-opus-5

Restart, and the header pill turns green.

Persistent data and durable jobs

docker compose up -d          # database + redis
MONGODB_URI=mongodb://localhost:27017/crm
REDIS_URL=redis://localhost:6379
npm run seed -w @crm/api      # add --reset to wipe

Embeddings and vector search

By default a small model runs inside the app and needs no key. Set VOYAGE_API_KEY or OPENAI_API_KEY to use a hosted one. For large note volumes, set PINECONE_API_KEY and PINECONE_INDEX.

Tuning

SettingDefaultEffect
RISK_INACTIVITY_DAYS14Silence before a deal counts as inactive
AI_TIMEOUT_MS45000How long an AI call may take before falling back
AI_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE30AI requests per user per minute
AI_CIRCUIT_FAILURES4Consecutive failures before the circuit opens
SMTP_URLunsetSet to actually deliver email; otherwise drafts are logged only

When AI is off

No feature disappears without a provider, and none of them break a screen. Each degrades to something honest and says so in the interface.

FeatureWithout a provider
Lead scoringSentiment comes from a keyword model. The score formula is unchanged.
Draft follow-upA stage-appropriate template, labelled as one.
Ask your CRMBuilt-in rules handle the common questions. Anything else says so.
Meeting summariesExtracted summary and commitment-style action items.
Semantic searchKeyword search, with the reason shown.
DuplicatesFull matching, minus the written verdict.
Risk flaggingThe same signals with a rule-based explanation.

The same applies when the provider is merely slow or erroring. A timeout falls back rather than hanging the page.

On a phone

The rail collapses into a scrolling row of links across the top, and the dashboard becomes a single column. Tables scroll sideways inside their own container, so the page itself never does.

Troubleshooting

Everything logged me out

The API restarted while running the in-memory database, so it reseeded with new accounts. Sign back in. Set a database URL to stop this.

A score or risk flag looks stale

Both update on a background job a moment after the change. Recompute on the deal page forces it. If nothing moves, check the circuit breaker on the AI usage page.

Semantic search says keyword fallback

Either nothing has been embedded yet, or the embedding model is still loading on first run, or the vector store is unreachable. Hover the status pill to see which.

A meeting stayed queued

Open it and use Retry. If the provider was down, the retry will pick it up once it recovers.

My question was rejected

The rejection text says why. Usually the question asked for a write, or for an aggregate the filter language cannot express. Rephrase it as a filter over deals or contacts.
